Delivery Manager – Biomechanics
Join Our Team at Sony Sports Technology
Value Stream: Biomechanics
Location: Hybrid working – minimum 2 days per week in the office
Office locations: Basingstoke, London or Bristol
Contract: Permanent, Full-Time

Hi, we're Amy Ogren and Robert Hulbert, and we're looking for a Delivery Manager to join our growing Biomechanics Value Stream. This is an exciting opportunity to join one of the fastest-growing areas within Sony Sports Technology. Our team combines Hawk-Eye's world-leading tracking technology with KinaTrax's markerless motion capture systems to provide cutting-edge athlete performance insights across elite sport.
You'll be joining a collaborative team of around 20 people that's expected to grow to approximately 25 over the coming year. Unlike many delivery roles that focus on a single product or sport, you'll support initiatives across Major League Baseball, the NFL, NBA, NHL, cricket, tennis and golf.
You'll also be joining at an exciting time as we continue delivering one of Sony Sports Technology's largest strategic partnerships while helping shape the future of biomechanics technology.

We're looking for someone who enjoys bringing people together, solving problems and helping technical teams deliver their best work.
As a Delivery Manager, you'll work closely with Product Managers, Engineering Leads, Solution Owners and software engineers to coordinate the delivery of technical initiatives across our biomechanics products.
You'll help keep projects moving by managing priorities, coordinating dependencies, identifying risks early and ensuring teams have the information they need to deliver successfully.
This isn't a traditional project management role. Priorities can change quickly as new opportunities emerge across multiple sports, so we're looking for someone who enjoys working in a collaborative, fast-paced environment where no two weeks are quite the same.
What You'll Work On
Supporting delivery across multiple biomechanics products and sports initiatives.
Coordinating work across engineering, product and operational teams.
Managing delivery roadmaps, milestones and project planning activities.
Supporting Agile ceremonies, sprint planning and delivery processes.
Tracking project progress and ensuring stakeholders have clear visibility of delivery.
Identifying risks, dependencies and blockers before they impact delivery.
Working closely with Product Managers, Engineering Leads and Solution Owners to coordinate priorities.
Helping improve delivery processes and ways of working across the Biomechanics Value Stream.
Building strong relationships with technical and business stakeholders across Sony Sports Technology.
What Success Looks Like
Your first few months will focus on learning the products, understanding how our teams work and building strong relationships across the business.
As your confidence grows, you'll begin taking ownership of delivery activities, supporting roadmap planning, identifying delivery risks and helping improve the way the team collaborates.
Success in this role isn't about changing everything on day one. It's about learning quickly, building trust and becoming someone the team relies on to help deliver complex technical projects successfully.

Coordinate the successful delivery of initiatives across the Biomechanics Value Stream.
Maintain delivery roadmaps, milestones and project timelines across multiple workstreams.
Facilitate Agile ceremonies including sprint planning, stand-ups, retrospectives and backlog refinement.
Track project dependencies, risks and blockers, ensuring they are managed proactively.
Support Product Managers and Engineering Leads with delivery planning and prioritisation.
Monitor delivery health and provide regular updates to stakeholders.
Escalate delivery risks with clear recommendations and proposed mitigation plans.
Help improve Agile delivery practices, team collaboration and operational efficiency.
Support cross-functional communication between engineering, product, operations and business teams.
Promote a culture of continuous improvement, transparency and accountability.
Skills, Knowledge & Experience

Experience supporting software, technical or product delivery within a technology environment.
An understanding of Agile delivery methodologies such as Scrum or Kanban.
Experience using Jira, Confluence or similar collaboration and planning tools.
Strong organisational, planning and prioritisation skills.
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
The ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Experience working alongside engineering or technical teams.
A proactive mindset with a passion for continuous improvement.
A genuine interest in technology and delivering high-quality products.

Exposure to sports technology or biomechanics.
Experience working across multiple technical teams.
An understanding of software development lifecycles.
A degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Sports Science, Biomechanics, Project Management or a related discipline is preferred, but not essential.

This is an opportunity to join one of the most exciting growth areas within Sony Sports Technology.
You'll work alongside experienced engineers, product managers and delivery specialists on technology that's helping redefine athlete performance analysis across professional sport.
As the Biomechanics Value Stream continues to expand, you'll have the opportunity to broaden your experience across multiple sports, contribute to high-profile programmes and develop your career within a growing global team.

Narvar is growing! We are hiring a Technical Project Manager to drive our most complex, multi-team engineering initiatives — the ones with no single owning team, where progress depends on getting the sequencing right across groups that don't naturally coordinate with each other.
This is not a status-reporting role. You won't be writing production code, but you will build and maintain the real dependency graph behind a project: which team's output blocks which other team's start, where the critical path actually runs, and what has to happen in what order for the whole thing to land.

You'll follow technical discussions closely enough to spot those dependencies before they become blockers, and you'll proactively pull in the right people — across engineering, product, design, data, or leadership — before gaps turn into delays.

Dependency mapping and critical path management
Map cross-team dependencies for projects that span multiple engineering teams with no single owning team — identify what blocks what, and in what order work needs to happen
Maintain a live view of the critical path, not just individual teams' task lists, and flag when a slip in one team changes the achievable timeline for others
Surface hidden or emerging dependencies before they become blockers, particularly ones that no single team has visibility into because they sit at the seams between teams
Distill the graph into concise, honest updates for non-technical stakeholders and leadership — what's driving the timeline, what's at risk, and why
Cross-functional coordination
Identify when product management, design, data, legal, or other stakeholders need to be looped in — and act on it proactively, without waiting for engineers to flag it
Recognize when a dependency crosses team boundaries and make sure the teams on both sides of it are actually talking to each other, not just individually on track
Chase down answers, escalate when needed, and keep work moving forward
Serve as the connective tissue across engineering and adjacent functions throughout the delivery lifecycle — especially where no single team is positioned to see the whole picture
Technical context and decision support
Follow technical discussions closely enough to grasp the tradeoffs being made — architecture decisions, infrastructure choices, API design, build vs. buy — and understand how those choices ripple into other teams' work
Reason about sequencing implications of technical decisions: does this choice change what can be built in parallel versus what must be serial?
Surface implications of technical decisions for timeline, scope, or other teams
Know when a decision warrants broader input and facilitate getting it, without creating unnecessary process overhead
Documentation and operational hygiene
Keep the dependency graph, specs, decisions, and timelines documented and accessible
Ensure decisions made in Slack or ad-hoc meetings don't get lost, especially ones that affect teams beyond the room they were made in
Make it easy for anyone joining a project mid-stream to get up to speed quickly — including understanding why the sequencing is what it is

Systems and dependency thinking: You can look at multiple teams' plans and identify where they interlock — where a change in one ripples into another — even when no one team has full visibility into the whole
Technical fluency: You don't need to write code, but you need to follow engineering conversations comfortably — architecture diagrams, system tradeoffs, sprint planning — without hand-holding
Project management experience: 4+ years managing complex, multi-team software projects with several workstreams and stakeholders in a fast-moving environment — ideally including projects with no single owning team
Strong written communication: Able to distill a complex dependency picture into crisp, accurate updates for non-technical audiences
Proactive by default: You identify when to loop someone in without being asked, and you follow through without needing to be chased
Calm under ambiguity: Able to drive clarity and keep work moving without waiting for perfect information, a fully defined process, or a single team to own the outcome
Cross-functional credibility: Comfortable holding a room with engineers, product managers, designers, and executives — and earning trust from all of them

Prior experience as a software engineer, QA, or technical analyst
Familiarity with agile and scrum methodologies; experience with tools like Jira, Linear, or Shortcut, especially for modeling cross-team dependencies
Experience running programs (not just single-team projects) — i.e., initiatives coordinated across multiple teams toward a shared outcome
Experience working with distributed or remote engineering teams

Die Stiftung Steinegg ist eine privatrechtliche soziale Institution in Wiesendangen (Raum Winterthur) die Wohn- und Arbeitsplätze für Menschen mit mehrfacher Beeinträchtigung anbietet. Wir legen grossen Wert auf Selbstbestimmung und unterstützende, fördernde Begleitung. Angeboten werden aktuell 36 Wohn- sowie rund 48 Tagesplätze. ## Bereichsleiter/in Agogik 60-80% Mitglied der Geschäftsleitung ##
In dieser Funktion übernehmen Sie die fachliche, personelle, finanzielle und organisatorische Leitung des Geschäftsbereichs Agogik, einschliesslich der Bereiche Wohnen und Tagesangebote sowie der Stabsstellen Gesundheit und Ausbildung, mit rund 60 Mitarbeitenden.

Ihr Ziel ist es, das gemeinsame agogische Verständnis und Handlungsfelder zu etablieren und weiterzuentwickeln.

Dazu erarbeiten Sie Konzepte und Instrumente zur praktischen Umsetzung der agogischen Grundlagen unter Einbezug der gegebenen betriebswirtschaftlichen Aspekte und stellen sicher, dass die Klienten die passenden, teilhabeorientierten Leistungen erhalten. Zudem sind Sie verantwortlich für die Erhebung des individuellen Betreuungsbedarfs (IBB).

Neben der fachlichen Führung tragen Sie in der Geschäftsleitung sowie in bereichsübergreifenden Projekten operative und strategische Mitverantwortung.
Wir wenden uns an eine führungserfahrene Persönlichkeit mit höherer Ausbildung und Berufserfahrung in Sozial- oder Heilpädagogik (FH).

Ihr breites Fachwissen konnten Sie mit Erfahrungen in komplexen Wohn- und/oder arbeitsagogischen Bereichen sowie mit Erfahrung im Umgang mit erwachsenen Menschen mit Beeinträchtigung und Verhaltensauffälligkeiten ergänzen. Ausserdem zeichnet Sie Ihr sicherer Umgang mit Konzeptarbeit und der daraus resultierenden Umsetzung aus.

Sie pflegen einen pragmatischen Ansatz und überzeugen durch Ihre integrative Art, verbunden mit Klarheit und sozialer Kompetenz. Dabei fördern Sie die interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit und einen offenen, wertschätzenden Umgang aller Beteiligten.Es erwartet Sie eine breit gefächerte Führungsaufgabe in einer in der Region gut verankerten Institution.

Bespoke Solutioning: Lead the strategic evolution of the implementation function to accommodate new business lines, innovative product offerings, and complex, bespoke customer needs, establishing scalable processes and best practices for diverse implementation challenges.

Project Manager, Client Onboarding
CrelioHealth Inc. · Remote (United States) · Full-time · Travel to client sites (~25–40%)
Compensation: $95,000 – $120,000 base, depending on experience + performance incentives (including incentives on expansion or referral opportunities you help close). Benefits include health coverage and PTO.
About CrelioHealth
CrelioHealth builds cloud-based laboratory information systems (LIS/LIMS) that power diagnostic labs across the United States and 2,500+ labs worldwide. Our platform runs the full lab workflow — from order booking and specimen tracking through result reporting, patient engagement, billing, and inventory — for physician office labs, hospital labs, reference labs, and direct-to-consumer testing companies. We are HIPAA-compliant, SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certified, and growing quickly in the US market.

When a lab signs with CrelioHealth , you are the person who turns that signature into a running lab. You will own client onboarding end to end: planning the implementation, configuring the rollout with our product and support teams, training lab staff, managing the go-live, and making sure the client is delighted enough to expand and refer. You are the face of CrelioHealth from kickoff to steady state.
This is not a sales role. You carry no quota and you will never cold-call. But onboarding is where trust is built, and trust is where growth comes from. We want someone who can confidently present the platform, handle a skeptical lab director, and spot the moment a client is ready for another module or another location — and who earns incentives when those opportunities convert.

Lead onboarding projects for new US clients — single-site labs through multi-location networks — from kickoff through go-live and handover to support.
Build and run the implementation plan: scope, milestones, data migration, instrument interfaces, integrations (EHR/EMR, billing, HL7/FHIR), user setup, and validation.
Coordinate internal teams (product, engineering, support) and client stakeholders (lab directors, pathologists, techs, front-desk, billing, IT) to keep every go-live on schedule.
Travel to client sites for kickoffs, go-lives, and training — roughly 25–40% of your time, varying with the project calendar.
Make clients successful
Train lab staff on real workflows — accessioning, worklists, QC, reporting, patient portal — and adapt the training to how each lab actually operates.
Anticipate and manage change resistance: a lab switching its LIS is changing how everyone works, and you will guide them through it.
Track onboarding health (time-to-go-live, adoption, early ticket volume) and report status honestly to clients and leadership.
Champion the platform
Present and demo CrelioHealth confidently — to the client team that signed, and to the wider staff who did not choose it but must love it.
Identify expansion opportunities during onboarding (additional modules, locations, or referrals) and hand them to the growth team — with incentives for you when they close.
Feed what you learn on the ground back into product and our onboarding playbook, which you will help write.

4–7 years of project management experience , with at least 2 years implementing or onboarding software for external clients.
Healthcare experience is required ; hands-on time in a clinical laboratory or laboratory environment is strongly preferred — as a lab tech, lab manager, LIS analyst, or implementer of lab systems (LIS/LIMS, EHR, RCM).
Fluency with lab operations concepts: specimen lifecycle, accessioning, QC/QA, instrument interfacing, CLIA/CAP context, HIPAA, and result reporting.
Excellent presenter and communicator — comfortable running a room of skeptical clinicians, and equally comfortable on a video call with a solo lab owner.
Structured and self-managing: you can run multiple concurrent onboardings remotely without anyone chasing you.
Willingness to travel to client sites across the US; valid driver’s license and authorization to work in the United States.
Nice-to-haves
Direct experience with an LIS/LIMS migration or go-live (any vendor).
Familiarity with HL7v2 / FHIR interfaces, lab billing/RCM basics, or instrument middleware.
Experience in customer success, solutions consulting, or pre-sales — anywhere you have had to win people over, not just manage tasks.
PMP, CAPM, or Lean Six Sigma is welcome but not required — we care more about go-lives you have shipped than certificates you hold.
Comfort using modern AI tools to work faster (drafting plans, summarizing calls, preparing training material) — with the judgment to know what still needs a human.
How We Hire
We know polished resumes and cover letters are easy to generate these days, so our process is built around watching you work rather than reading about it. After a screening call, you will do a live onboarding simulation based on a realistic lab scenario, and a short role-play where you present CrelioHealth to a (friendly but skeptical) “lab director.” No trick questions, no take-home busywork — just the actual job, compressed. We will respect your time and give you a decision quickly.
The Fine Print

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.

Für den Ausbau unserer teilbegleiteten Übergangswohnangebote für Frauen und Kinder im Anschluss an den Frauenhausaufenthalt suchen wir Verstärkung in der Funktion Projektleitung (40%).
## Projektleiterin Übergangswohnen (40%) ##
Eintritt per sofort oder nach Vereinbarung, befristet auf 9 Monate mit Möglichkeit zur Verlängerung
Du gestaltest den Ausbau und die Weiterentwicklung unserer Übergangswohnangebote massgeblich mit.
Deine Aufgaben
* Du entwickelst das Fach- und Betriebskonzept sowie die organisatorischen und finanziellen Grundlagen weiter
* Du planst, koordinierst und steuerst die nächsten Umsetzungsschritte.
* Du entwickelst Prozesse, Standards und Arbeitsinstrumente
* Du verantwortest die Suche, Prüfung und Bereitstellung geeigneter Wohnlösungen.
* Du koordinierst die Zusammenarbeit mit Behörden, Fachstellen und Partnerorganisationen
* Du wirkst an der nachhaltigen Verankerung und Weiterentwicklung des Angebots mit.
Was du mitbringst
* Hochschulabschluss in Sozialer Arbeit, Sozialwissenschaften oder einem verwandten Fachgebiet
* Erfahrung in der Projektleitung und Angebotsentwicklung im sozialen Bereich
* Kenntnisse in den Bereichen häusliche Gewalt, Opferhilfe und/oder begleitete Wohnformen von Vorteil
* Konzeptionelle Stärke und eine strukturierte, selbständige Arbeitsweise
* Kommunikationsstärke und Freude an Vernetzung und Zusammenarbeit
* Freude daran, ein wachsendes Angebot mitzugestalten
Was wir dir bieten
* Sinnstiftende Arbeit mit viel Gestaltungsspielraum
* Ein engagiertes Team mit gegenseitiger Unterstützung
* Intervision, Supervision und Weiterbildung
* Faire Anstellungsbedingungen und gute Sozialleistungen
